newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-West Indies humiliated before Test.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-West Indies humiliated before Test.

text.p: West Indies on Monday slumped to a crushing 10-wicket defeat in their final warm-up match to complete a dismal preparation for the first test against Australia, starting in Brisbane on Friday.
Former test all-rounder Greg Blewett snared a career-best five for 29 as the tourists were humiliated by an Australian XI team featuring a host of fringe test players.
But West Indies coach Malcolm Marshall played down the significance of the heavy and untimely defeat, just four days before first ball is bowled at the Gabba.
"We have struggled at the start of tours before and played well in the first test. You shouldn't try to read too much into it and I'm sure we'll be firing come Friday," Marshall said.
West Indies failed to bat through the day on Monday to salvage a draw after being forced to follow on in reply to the home side's massive first innings 544 for four declared.
Victoria opener Mathew Elliot, who scored 158 in the first innings, celebrated his selection for the first test by guiding the Australia XI to victory on Monday.
After being dismissed for 317, West Indies scored 251 in their second innings, leaving the home side to chase a paltry target of 25 runs for victory.
Elliot, who replaced opener Michal Slater in the test line-up, easily completed the task in partnership with Matthew Hayden, scorer of a brilliant double century in the first innings.
Blewett was a member of Australia's tour party for their series win against West Indies in the Caribbean last year but has since fallen out of favour with selectors.
He took five wickets at cost of just 12 runs after lunch on Monday to destroy West Indies middle and lower and order.
But there was some encouragement for West Indies with Shivnarine Chanderpaul and Brian Lara both scoring half-centuries to delay the outcome.
Fast bowler Jason Gillespie, who failed to take a wicket in West Indies' second innings, and batsman Michael Bevan joined Elliot in Australia's 12-man squad for the first test.
